Generation unprepared: The school and university leavers with no skills to work at all

That really isn't too surprising. When employers demand higher education for even the most menial of jobs it pushes people into full-time schooling and away from those part-time jobs in their youth. Now the employers are complaining as they get people who are fully credentialed but have never held a real job and need to be taught the expectations of the workforce.

Maybe if these employers (and note the one featured in the article is in the mining industry, not exactly known for needing an advanced degree for most workers) were willing to train people on the job they would be able to find non-credentialed but work-experienced employees.

That is a good idea, it's implementation can be sticky though, as a company can invest the time and money into an employee only to find out that that employee was simply using that training as experience to get a better job. It is a risky proposition for the training company, and they would be forced into somehow ensuring that the employee stayed for some predetermined set of time (contract, no-compete etc...) which some employees find risky themselves. But I give you points for presenting a thoughtful response and potential solution. I have missed them on Voat today...

You are right, the risk of the employee taking the training and leaving is high. On the flip side, other than general experience and practice, most on-the-job training is rather company-specific so is of limited use when jumping ship. Also, while a new hire will be working at a lower capacity during training, they will still be productive so it's not like the company get nothing for their investment.

You also see that take-the-training-and-run think in the education-required fields too, especially in IT.
